source_tasks.problem: The expression $4 \times  5 +  2 -  8 -  3 +  3 \times  5$ may be changed only by inserting parentheses; rearranging numbers or operations is not allowed. In total, how many values can be obtained?

Consider the expression $4 +  8 -  6 \cdot  6 -  4 +  2 \cdot  7$. Fully parenthesize it in every possible way without changing the order of numbers or operations. Parenthesizations with the same numerical result count only once. How many distinct values are possible?
The expression $7 +  6 \times  8 -  6 +  5 \times  3 -  5$ may be changed only by inserting parentheses; rearranging numbers or operations is not allowed. In total, how many values can be obtained?

interface_note: Only parameter values vary; all mathematical conditions and requested quantity remain those stated by the supplied source questions. Names describe source data, not a target algorithm. Implement solve(parameters), no natural-language applicability detection. operators must have exactly len(operands)-1 entries.

observations: Each source question asks for the number of distinct values obtainable by fully parenthesizing a fixed sequence of integers and binary operators +,-,* without reordering.
The requested quantity is the cardinality of the set of results over all full binary parenthesizations of the operator sequence.
The parameter schema supplies operands and operators with len(operators)=len(operands)-1, matching the fixed sequence structure.
Because only +,-,* are used, all intermediate and final values are integers, so distinct values can be tracked exactly in a set.
The number of full parenthesizations grows Catalan-like, but dynamic programming over contiguous operand intervals avoids enumerating duplicate parenthesizations explicitly.
analysis.procedure_plan: Implement solve(parameters): read operands a[0..n-1] and operators op[0..n-2]. Define DP[i][j] as the set of all integer values obtainable by fully parenthesizing the subexpression a[i] op[i] ... op[j-1] a[j]. Base case DP[i][i]={a[i]}. For length L from 2 to n, for each i with j=i+L-1, initialize DP[i][j]=empty set. For each split k from i to j-1, combine every x in DP[i][k] with every y in DP[k+1][j] using op[k]: if '+', add x+y; if '-', add x-y; if '*', add x*y. Insert results into DP[i][j]. Return the size of DP[0][n-1]. Use exact integer arithmetic and sets for deduplication.
analysis.uncertainty: The plan assumes the source questions' phrase 'inserting parentheses' is equivalent to considering all full binary parenthesizations of the given left-to-right sequence, which is the standard interpretation. If a source intended only some restricted class of parenthesizations, the count could differ, but the supplied statements do not indicate such a restriction.
